title: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
abstract: arXiv:2610.18853v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) relies on costly model-generated responses, motivating larger rollout batches and square-root learning-rate scaling. Reported to approximately preserve progress per sample with one optimizer step per rollout, this rule is less understood in practical multi-step training. We develop a two-clock framework that separates the samples needed to make progress from those consumed before collapse. Under a local quadratic model, the square-root rule preserves first-order drift per sample but not progress: larger batches take fewer, longer updates and lose more to curvature, yielding a learning-rate-dependent critical batch beyond which sample efficiency degrades. A drift-threshold hypothesis predicts a complementary failure clock whose sample count remains approximately invariant along the square-root rule. translated_title: 双时钟：为何更大的 rollout 批次学习更慢却在可验证奖励强化学习中如期失效
translated_abstract: 可验证奖励强化学习依赖于代价高昂的模型生成响应，这促使研究者采用更大的 rollout 批次和平方根学习率缩放。据已有报告，在每次 rollout 执行一次优化器更新的设定下，该规则可近似保持每个样本的进度，但在实际的多步训练中，人们对它的理解仍然不足。我们提出了一个“双时钟”框架，将“取得进展所需的样本量”与“崩溃之前所消耗的样本量”区分开来。在局部二次模型下，平方根规则保持的是每个样本的一阶漂移，而非真正的进度：更大的批次执行次数更少但单次更长的更新，并在曲率上损失更多，从而产生一个依赖于学习率的临界批次，超过该批次后样本效率便会下降。一个漂移阈值假设进一步预测存在一个互补的失效时钟，其样本数量在平方根规则下保持近似不变。在 Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B 上跨越 16 倍批次范围的受控 GRPO 实验支持了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出“双时钟”理论框架，解释了在可验证奖励强化学习中，平方根学习率缩放虽保持每样本的一阶漂移却无法保持真实进度，因而更大的 rollout 批次因曲率损失导致样本效率下降，而崩溃失效点在样本数量上保持近似不变。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a two-clock framework showing that under square-root learning-rate scaling in RLVR, larger rollout batches preserve per-sample first-order drift but not true progress—losing efficiency to curvature—while the collapse point remains approximately invariant in sample count.
